title: Project Management
subtitle: Delivering on time and on scope

terms.hint: What's in (and out of) the project
The money you have to work with

questions.q: New 'must-have' features keep getting added mid-project. This is…
options: Scope creep — manage it via change control
questions.explain: Uncontrolled additions blow timelines and budgets. Capture changes and re-agree scope explicitly.

questions.q: What's the point of a daily stand-up?
options: A quick sync on progress, plans and blockers
questions.explain: Short and focused: what's done, what's next, what's blocking. Solve details afterwards.

options: Identify risks early and plan responses
questions.explain: Naming risks early lets you mitigate or plan for them before they bite.

questions.q: Task B can't start until Task A finishes. Task A is a…
questions.explain: B depends on A. Mapping dependencies reveals the critical path through the work.

questions.q: Best way to handle a slipping deadline?
options: Flag it early and discuss scope, time or resource trade-offs
questions.explain: Surface slippage early so stakeholders can choose the trade-off consciously.
Clear, dated milestones make progress visible and honest.
